title: decision.v1 payload
description: A decision emitted by a stock decision engine for a single ticker, across three independent horizons. This is a data contract, not a model: it carries the decision and its price context, never the inputs that produced it. Producers disagree about permissible inputs (one is technical-only by rule, the other blends fundamentals) and that disagreement is deliberate on both sides, so no field here may require an input only one producer can supply. Short, mid and long are fully independent; a consumer must never average or vote across them, and this contract deliberately expresses no overall action.

contractVersion.description: Exact match. Any other value is rejected outright, never best-effort parsed as v1.

ticker.description: Normalized listed-equity symbol. Same pattern as contracts/portfolio-research, allowing plain tickers and common share-class suffixes (e.g. BRK.B).

generatedAt.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp, Z-suffixed. When the producer computed this decision, not when it was transmitted.

currentPrice.description: The price the producer evaluated against, as of generatedAt. Lives in the envelope rather than per-horizon because it is one value per snapshot: the horizons differ in their ranges, not in the price they are compared to. Null only when the producer had no usable quote, in which case every horizon must report an unusable landscape.

producer.description: Which engine emitted this decision. Required because this contract has two producers, and the consuming agreement layer must be able to tell them apart to report concurrence or disagreement.

id.description: Stable producer slug. Not a closed enum, so a third engine does not require a contract version bump; the pattern prevents casing and separator drift (analyst-service, never Analyst_Service) so the consumer can compare ids reliably. Known values today: 'analyst-service' (this repo) and 'stock-decision-dashboard'.

engineVersion.description: Producer-defined model or build version, for attributing a change in behaviour to a change in the engine. Optional: a producer with no version concept emits null rather than a placeholder.

horizons.description: All three horizons are always present and always independent. A producer that cannot evaluate a horizon still emits it, reporting an unusable landscape, rather than omitting the key: a missing horizon and a horizon with no opinion are different states, and only the second is honest.

priceRange.description: An inclusive price band. JSON Schema cannot express low < high, nor opportunityRange.high < reduceRange.low, because both are cross-field numeric comparisons; those two invariants are enforced by contracts/decision/tests, not here.

horizonDecision.description: One horizon's complete decision. Every field is required, including the nullable ones: a producer must state that it has no opportunity range rather than omit the key, so a consumer can distinguish 'no zone' from 'field not implemented'.

action.description: What to do. Constrained by priceState via the allOf rules below.

confidence.description: Support consistency and stability of the decision, NOT a calibrated probability. A consumer must not read this as a likelihood of the action being profitable, and must not compare it across producers as if both were calibrated.

priceState.description: Where currentPrice sits relative to this horizon's price structure. This is the gate on action, not a decoration computed after it.

executionIntent.description: How to act on the position, as distinct from the directional call. Not gated against action by this schema; see contracts/decision/README.md open questions.

opportunityRange.description: The band in which a positive action is permitted. Null when no usable zone could be formed. Never widen this to make a decision expressible: an absent zone is an honest answer.

reduceRange.description: The band in which trimming or selling is permitted. Null when no usable zone could be formed.

invalidation.description: Price at which this horizon's thesis is structurally wrong. Null when the producer cannot derive one. Not a stop-loss recommendation and not position sizing.

allOf.description: IN_OPPORTUNITY_ZONE permits only the positive action family. Being in the zone never automatically creates a buy; the producer chooses intensity within the family.
The neutral band and both near-zones are informational only. They may shape reasons and confidence but can never trigger an early entry or an early reduction.
Inside or beyond the reduce band, every positive action is prohibited and so is hold. A producer that wants hold here must rebuild its landscape rather than add an exception.
A confirmed breakdown permits an exit or avoidance. Price being high alone is not a breakdown.
With no usable landscape the producer may only decline to act. It must also emit null ranges rather than fabricate fake-precision bands.

reasons.description: Bounded free text. Both producers emit prose reasons today, so a closed reason-code enum would be invented rather than derived; revisit once real strings from both engines can be compared. Both arrays are required and may be empty.

dataQuality.description: Whether this horizon's inputs were good enough to trust the decision. Vocabulary reuses contracts/portfolio-research's status values rather than inventing a parallel set.

state.description: 'partial' means the decision stands on incomplete inputs and confidence should already reflect that. 'unavailable' means no decision could be formed, and priceState is expected to be INVALID_LANDSCAPE.
